comparison: Both evaluate claims C4, C17, C18, C19 about CD8+ T cell clonal expansion in αKO tumors. OpenEval finds the claims well-supported by scRNA-seq and TCR data. Peer reviewers raise critical concerns about limited sample size (n=2 hosts), lack of functional validation for tumor specificity, and recommend softening language from 'expansion' to 'enrichment'. Major disagreement on sufficiency of evidence.

Both evaluate claims C5, C21-C23, C27-C31 about CRISPR screen identification of Pccb. OpenEval finds strong support from screen data and validation experiments. Peer reviewers express concerns about limited screen success (2/8 tumors), inadequate statistical power, and fundamental concern that results may be based on a single tumor clone with confounding changes beyond PIK3CA deletion. Significant disagreement on robustness.

OpenEval evaluates C32-C38 (metabolic characterization) as supported, while peer review focuses on C35-C38. OpenEval finds multiple assays support lack of metabolic changes. Peer reviewer challenges this conclusion, noting trends in OCR and αKG that lack significance due to high variability and small sample size (n=3), suggesting experimental error rather than true lack of difference. Disagreement on interpretation of negative results.

Both evaluate claims C39-C44 about T cell exhaustion markers. OpenEval finds IHC and flow cytometry data well-support increased checkpoint expression, though notes functional assays would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers identify methodological concerns: lack of normalization to total CD8+ counts in quantification, incomplete flow cytometry (single replicate), and criticism of IHC technique. Agreement on general finding but disagreement on methodological rigor.

Both evaluate PD1 blockade therapeutic response (C45-C48, C66-C68). OpenEval finds strong support from survival data and imaging with appropriate controls. Peer reviewer agrees it is 'reasonable to conclude' p-αKO tumors respond to checkpoint blockade, but notes limitation that anti-PD1 data in αKO tumors were not included for comparison. General agreement with minor reservations.

Both evaluate claims C49-C56, C69 about T cell reactivation by PD1 blockade. OpenEval finds scRNA-seq and TCR data well-support reactivation of anti-tumor T cells. Peer reviewer fundamentally challenges the interpretation, stating 'there is no data presented to support' that checkpoint blockade reactivates existing responses rather than inducing de novo responses, noting lack of confirmed tumor-specific TCR tracking. Major disagreement on mechanistic interpretation despite technical data quality.

OpenEval evaluates C57-C58 about Tpex to effector memory transition as supported by scRNA-seq, though notes lineage tracing would strengthen conclusions. Peer review of overlapping claim C58 challenges broader mechanistic claims about reactivation versus de novo responses. Partial overlap with different emphasis on evidence gaps.

Both evaluate claims C59-C61 about human patient data correlations. OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting C59 lacks significance (p=0.19) and C61 significance unclear, requiring validation. Peer reviewers do not raise specific concerns and appear to accept these correlative findings. OpenEval is more critical of statistical limitations than peer review.

OpenEval evaluates C80-C81 about metabolite measurements (MC, C3, propionyl-CoA) as uncertain due to lack of statistical significance and technical limitations acknowledged by authors. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific metabolite claims.

Both evaluate mechanistic claims C90-C91 about PCCB regulation of immune evasion. OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting inferential leaps and lack of direct demonstration of PD-L1 regulation. Peer reviewer (R3) directly challenges main conclusions, arguing no clear evidence PCCB deletion modulates CD8 T cell activity and suggesting alternative interpretation (reduced immunogenicity). Both identify major gaps but peer review is more fundamentally skeptical.
OpenEval evaluates C1, C2, C8-C12 as supported background knowledge about PDAC with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these standard background claims.

OpenEval evaluates C3, C13-C16, C62-C64 as supported prior published work accurately represented with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature context claims.
OpenEval evaluates C24-C26, C78-C79 as supported established biochemistry of PCC with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these biochemical background claims.
OpenEval evaluates C70-C72, C75-C76 as supported prior work on combination therapies with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these therapeutic context claims.

OpenEval evaluates C77 about TIGIT and LAG3 elevation as supported by IHC data, with reasonable inference about additional checkpoint inhibitors. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates C82-C86 as supported prior work on propionate's immune effects with appropriate citations, noting conflicting findings in literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic context claims.
OpenEval evaluates C20, C88-C89 as supported methodological and novelty statements with appropriate justification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological claims.

Peer review evaluates claim C7 (not covered by OpenEval) along with therapeutic response claims. C7 appears to be an additional claim about experimental design or context not separately evaluated by OpenEval.
